notes: Roadmap brief. The build (Phases 0-5) is closed; the roadmap is now four promise-gates. Gate-driven, no dates (no-timelines rule). Companion audio in the same folder. Theme: boardroom.

blocks.text: The machine is built. Now we prove it and roll it out.
2026-07-05 - prepared for Henry Burden - all six build phases are closed; the road ahead is four promise-gates, and Gate 2 (prove it on a real repo) is the one in flight.

footer: Board is the live source of truth: github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents (project #9)

blocks.text: The extender pipeline - one source copy per primitive, rendered to Claude Code and opencode with a drift guard - is fully built. This session turned a loosely-ranked board into a gated plan: 12 issues all conformant and labeled, four promise-gates fully binned, and the pilot's own tail scoped honestly.

items: Build closed: Phases 0-5 done, scaffold through bootstrap - the plumbing works; proving and rollout remain
The roadmap is now four gates: Pilot proven (active), Lifecycle live, Rollout and retire, and a new Cross-tool parity gate for the move off Claude-Code-as-baseline
The active job is Gate 2: prove project-workflow on a real repo - now hsb3/fleet-dashboard (#33), the one item in flight; raptorgpt is the completed prior pilot
The pilot's tail is honest now: the toolkit bug (#68) is confirmed live, and two over-reaching issues (#69, #70) were re-scoped to their true residual against current source

footer: Counts as-of 2026-07-05; live counts belong to the board

blocks.text: A ranked board and a gated plan
The pipeline is built and drift-guarded - what's left is proving, not plumbing

items: One source copy per primitive, rendered into per-target bundles
Translation service renders targets; a CI drift guard fails on hand-edits
The workbench promotion gate (unproven to proven) and clean-machine bootstrap both land
All six construction phases closed and their milestones retired

Cross-tool parity (#59) - agnostic base format, gated on its own decisions
hsb3-custom-plugins not yet retired - waits on the symlink + commands migration (#32)

footer: Milestones are promise-gates: a gate is safe to claim only when its issues close

blocks.text: Four promise-gates turn the backlog into a sequenced plan

items: Gate 2 - Pilot proven: 5 open - the current job, led by the fleet-dashboard pilot #33
Gate P1 - Lifecycle live: 3 open - the consolidation migration #32 + extender curation
gate:cross-tool and gate:consolidation labels track the two hard blockers
Gate 3 - Rollout and retire: 3 open - externals #36, ra-platform commands #37, pw v2 #27
Gate 4 - Cross-tool parity: 1 open - agnostic base format #59, filed this session
No hard blockers open: the constraints are owner decisions, not code dependencies

footer: Gating chain: fleet-dashboard pilot #33 -> Gate 2 -> consolidation #32 -> Gate 3 rollout

blocks.text: Everything downstream keys off Gate 2 closing

items: In flight: the Gate-2 pilot (#33) - run audit, scaffold, and re-audit on hsb3/fleet-dashboard and route findings; raptorgpt is the completed prior pilot
Clears with it: the roster provenance field (#39) and the three planning-desk self-fixes (#68, #69, #70) - the standards fixes the pilot surfaced
Then ready: the symlink + commands migration (#32) that unblocks retiring hsb3-custom-plugins - the one other build-ready item
Parallel bet: the agnostic base format (#59) - high impact, extra-large, plan-and-decompose next; it makes opencode parity real

footer: Deliverables + parallelism, not durations; the objective is a gate, not a date

blocks.text: What could slip the objective or bite right after

items: The pilot tail is self-referential: planning-desk fails its own standards when dogfooded - cheap to fix, but the signal that 'proven' is not yet true
The agnostic base format (#59) is extra-large and shares open decisions with externals (#36) - do not start either before its decisions close
No hard blockers, so the risk is drift: owner decisions are the bottleneck, and a stale rank hides in a big backlog - re-run triage rather than trusting a snapshot
The brief itself is a local working artifact (gitignored) - it will not travel in a clone unless negated

blocks.text: The pipeline is built; the work now is to prove it on a real repo, consolidate, and roll it out - four gates, no dates.
